# Copilot instructions for this repo

Overview
- **Project type:** PlatformIO-based ESP8266 project using the Arduino framework (see `platformio.ini`).
- **Primary board/env:** `nodemcuv2` (see `[env:nodemcuv2]`).

Quick goals for an AI agent
- **Understand build contexts:** Read `platformio.ini` first to discover environment names, platforms, frameworks and `lib_deps` pins.
- **Keep changes minimal:** Follow PlatformIO conventions: put source in `src/`, headers in `include/`, libraries in `lib/` or `lib_deps`.

Key files & patterns to inspect
- `platformio.ini`: single source of truth for build/upload/monitor settings. Example in this repo:
  - `platform = espressif8266`, `board = nodemcuv2`, `framework = arduino`, `monitor_speed = 9600`.
  - `lib_deps` lists pinned libraries (Blynk v1.3.2, WiFiManager v2.0.17).
- `src/` directory: runtime sources belong here (the folder is currently empty). Add `main.cpp` or `.ino` files here.
- `include/` and `lib/`: project headers and local libraries; `lib/README` may contain local library guidance.
- `test/` (if used): PlatformIO unit tests; currently contains a README.

Developer workflows (commands an agent should use)
- Build: `pio run -e nodemcuv2` (or `platformio run -e nodemcuv2`).
- Upload to device: `pio run -t upload -e nodemcuv2`.
- Serial monitor: `pio device monitor -b 9600` or `pio run -e nodemcuv2 -t monitor` (note `monitor_speed` in `platformio.ini`).
- Add/upgrade libraries: edit `lib_deps` in `platformio.ini` and run `pio update` / `pio run` to fetch and build.

Project-specific conventions
- Prefer explicit env usage: always reference the env name (e.g., `-e nodemcuv2`) rather than relying on defaults.
- Library pins: Keep `lib_deps` version specifiers intact unless updating intentionally—these pins stabilize CI/boards.
- Framework choices: An alternate env (`modwifi`) using `esp8266-rtos-sdk` is present but commented; do not switch frameworks without coordination.

Integration points to watch
- Blynk and WiFiManager: configuration and network flows likely depend on secrets/config data — do not commit credentials. Look for runtime config locations (filesystem, `include/`, or sketches in `src/`).
- Serial I/O: many debugging flows use the serial monitor at 9600 baud (see `monitor_speed`).

When changing code
- Add new source files to `src/`. Keep `main()`-style entrypoint simple and move platform-agnostic logic to additional modules under `src/` or `lib/`.
- Update `platformio.ini` only when adding new boards, changing frameworks, or modifying library pins.

What this agent should NOT do
- Do not add credentials or secret keys to the repository. If required, stub them and document how a developer provides real values at runtime.
- Do not change the commented `modwifi` env to active without confirming intent — it's an alternate RTOS-based configuration.

If you need more detail
- Ask for the main application file(s) that will run on the device (placeholders in `src/`), or provide a short sample of expected behavior (network setup, Blynk interactions) so instructions can be extended with concrete code examples.
